newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares break resistance ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares break resistance ahead of expiry.

text.p: Austrian shares closed sharply higher on Thursday after breaking through a key resistance level that had kept the market confined to a narrow range for seven weeks.
Traders said further gains had been prevented by uncertainty ahead of Friday's expiry of futures and options contracts on the ATX index and its main constituents.
The ATX index rose 14.81 points or 1.44 percent to close at 1,045.54, its highest level since mid-July. Ever since, the ATX has been moved in a tight range between 1,020 and 1,040 points.
All but one of the index members finished higher.

Traders said the market was well supported technically. "The ATX and several of its constituents look pretty good from a technical point of view," said one. "If you are a chartist, you'd have to buy now."
Mayr-Melnhof Karton lead the day's decliners, rising 3.85 percent or 20 schillings to 540.
Among financial shares, insurer EA-Generali was up 98 schillings at 2,985. The group leads a consortium of bidders for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt.
The bank's ordinary shares were up 17 schillings at 637, while its preference stock rose 9.60 schillings to 467.10.
Finance Minister Viktor Klima is expected to announce his final decision on EA-Generali's bid for the government's 70 percent voting stake in the bank before the end of the week.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index rose 4.33 points or 1.1 percent to close at 406.24.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for September delivery were up 15 points at 1,047.0.
